 Pennsylvanians on Social Security need more than an adjustment [column] 
 BILL JOHNSTON-WASH | COMMENTARY 
 Nov 14, 2026 
 1 hr ago 
 Bill Johnston-Walsh
 Submitted 
 Facebook 
-->
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
-->
 Twitter 
 Email 
 Print 
 Copy article link 
 For millions of Pennsylvanians, the annual Social Security cost of living adjustment is more than a number. It’s a lifeline for paying rent, buying groceries, making home repairs and covering car payments. And for too many residents here in the commonwealth, their monthly payment isn’t keeping up with the increasing cost of living in 2026.
 The federal government recently announced a 3.6% Social Security COLA, which, for the average Social Security recipient, means an additional $900 per year. Much of that news got lost with the recent midterm elections, but it’s worth remembering that while the COLA helps, for too many older Americans, it is not keeping pace with the rising costs of everyday life.
 A recent AARP survey of older adults found most adults ages 50 and over (76%) say the COLA increase for 2027 does not seem like it is keeping up with rising prices — attitudes that have remained consistent in recent years.
 Across Pennsylvania, people tell us they are feeling the pressure. Groceries cost more. Utility bills consume a larger share of monthly budgets. Health care and prescription drug costs continue to strain families. For someone living on a fixed income, even a modest increase in costs can force difficult choices that reverberate through our economy.
 One in five Pennsylvanians — more than 3 million residents — receive a Social Security payment. The average payment is $2,142 monthly, or $25,707 annually. These payments inject $71.8 billion into the state’s economy every year.
 Social Security recipients paid into it with every paycheck. They earned it through decades of hard work. This money belongs to them, and they depend on it.

 Half of Social Security recipients say it is their main source of income, and most Americans 50 and over say the 2027 COLA increase will not keep up with rising prices, according to AARP research. That means that, even with an adjustment, too many older Americans still feel like they’re falling behind.
 Yet special interests in Washington, D.C., continue to push ideas that would reduce or cut the COLA. These proposals are out of touch with the reality facing older Americans in communities across our state.
 The upcoming COLA matters because every dollar matters. But protecting Americans from rising prices requires more than an annual adjustment. It requires protecting and strengthening the Social Security benefits Americans have earned.
 Congress must act to ensure Social Security is there for today’s retirees and for the generations still paying into it with every paycheck, without cutting the money they have earned.
 Pennsylvania’s message is simple: Keep the promise. Protect and strengthen Social Security for the Americans who earned it.
 Bill Johnston-Walsh is the state director of AARP Pennsylvania.
